cells.tense: You are standing where the weight settles and it holds.
cells.act: follow the thought past where it is comfortable
cells.ask: Take a worry you keep at arm's length and follow it one step deeper than usual. One step, no notes, nobody told.
cells.core:
You can look straight at something and carry it in the same hour. The weight lands, your eyes stay open, and neither one spends the other. Nothing has to be resolved for you to keep noticing what's actually around you while you hold your end of the load up.

Take a worry you usually keep at arm's length and follow it one step past where you'd stop. Just the single step. Something turns up there — a pattern, an edge, the real shape underneath. That depth isn't a prize for gritting through. It's what opens when whatever holds you steady is steady enough to look from.
cells.sheetLine: You can look at it and carry it, same hour.
cells.verb: seeing clearly before the shape forms

cells.tense: You are bracing against a weight that has not landed yet.
cells.act: complete what you began by beginning it
cells.ask: Choose a thing you're braced for and do its smallest first piece today. The start only, then close the day.
cells.core:
You can already see what's coming, and you've taken most of it onto your shoulders before it arrives. The heaviest part of your load is forecast — a future you're carrying in advance. That's a strong back running ahead of its own day. When it's going well, you meet what's actually here: the email that exists, the call that's real, the morning you're actually in. Each moment arrives fresh and you handle it fresh.

Select a thing you're braced for and do only the smallest first piece of it today. The start, nothing after. Begin it on the day you're actually in, and let the rest of the forecast wait until it's real. What lands then lands on somebody already standing.
cells.sheetLine: Most of what you're carrying hasn't happened yet.
cells.verb: seeing clearly before the shape forms

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door you walked through already.
cells.act: complete the form so it stands without you
cells.ask: Name some finished piece of work and set it down where it finished. The sentence is the whole assignment.
cells.core:
What you're gripping is already over, and you keep reaching back for it. The door closed behind you and part of you stayed in the frame. Not weakness — long practice at holding on, still running after the thing let go. Your attention lives in the hallway behind you more than in the place you're standing.

Name some finished piece of work: done, closed, behind. Say what it was in three words to yourself and set it down where it finished. That's the seal. What you built stands without your shoulder under it, and there's an afternoon here you haven't been in for a while.
cells.sheetLine: It's finished. You're still holding your shoulder under it.
cells.verb: seeing clearly before the shape forms

cells.tense: You are steering the room and filing it as temperament.
cells.act: notice what is newly here, right now
cells.ask: Stop once today, catch something present now that wasn't this morning, give it a word, move on.
cells.core:
You read the shift in a face before it's spoken, the change in a tone before the sentence ends. That kind of attention runs all day, and on your own account it just happens to you — temperament, tiredness, knowing how people are. The attention is yours. Your name on it isn't.

Once today, stop and catch something here now that wasn't here this morning. The angle of the light, a sound that just started, somebody standing differently. Give it a word, one time, and keep moving. A thing you noticed is a thing you did, and saying so is how the doing gets handed back to you.
cells.sheetLine: What you noticed is yours, filed under temperament.
cells.verb: seeing clearly before the shape forms
